But is this a bad thing or does it mean new opportunities arise? What do the tech tycoons like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg have to say about it? And which jobs will disappear? Stay tuned to hear all about it!. Welcome to World Econ News, your daily dose of economics and finance. If you are interested in topics influencing the world economies and global financial flows, this is the place for you! Watch till the end if you want to get the latest on everything! And don’t forget to Subscribe, Like, and Hit the notification button to get the latest updates! Let’s go…! Get out of your comfort zone, this is a serious issue. Artificial Intelligence aka “Ai” is stealing your job. Does not matter what field or sector you are in, smart machines and software programs are already putting millions out of work every year. It is happening and governments are not doing anything about it. Why? In the name of progress. However, most sane unbiased experts who care about people more than reckless unregulated billionaires-led progress, “it is all about the super-rich getting richer”. Here is a real scary figure about this widely ignored truth. According to a report by the World Economic Forum “WEF” issued in 2020 “The rise of machines and automation would globally eliminate a huge 85 million jobs by 2025”. The report goes on to state that there are also “mere expectations” that 97 million jobs will be created due to progress in AI and automation during the same period hence 12 million jobs will be added. Then the same report says “that by 2025 work will be divided equally among humans and machines”. This sounded confusing, so, I spoke to some analysts, and they said, only the first figure in the report is true and things could be worse. As for the other figures, “it seems the report writers are trying to create confusion in order to please their institution’s 1000 corporate members, who fund the WEF”. Alright, you probably want more evidence, right? Check this out, in the past 2 years, more than 40 million people in the world’s richest countries, left their jobs voluntarily to become their own bosses. Nevertheless, the governments of these countries along with the corporate giants and the media did not seem to mind at all. Life went on as if nothing happened. Do you want to know why? This presented an opportunity for all corporations in all sectors to begin implementing their plans of substituting human workers with Ai-powered machines and programs, which saves them not billions, but trillions of dollars in wages every year. Allow me now to stun you with a figure. In the U.S.A alone. Ai and smart automation save companies “$2.7 trillion in wages” annually. Yes, that’s in the trillions, and that was before more than 20 million Americans quit their jobs over the past 2 years. Ok, ok, relax, you have some doubts and want some solid proof. No worries, you got it. Now listen to what the technology tycoons are saying. “These are their own words” not mine. Elon Musk said that the job losses would be so severe, the government would be forced to pay people to live. He said: “There is a pretty good chance we end up with a universal basic income, or something like that, due to automation,” - “Yeah, I am not sure what else one would do. I think that is what would happen”. Facebook founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg promoted the idea of universal basic income during his commencement speech to Harvard in May 2021. He said: “Now it’s our time to define a new social contract for our generation. We should explore ideas like universal basic income to give everyone a cushion to try new things,”. I think he meant giving everyone some time and space to piss off, stay home using Facebook and the Metaverse while waiting for the next welfare check along with some charity from the Salvation Army. Bill Gates said: “Robots taking over our jobs will make us more efficient, and lead to more free time.” - “Well, certainly we can look forward to the idea that vacations will be longer at some point," - "If we can actually produce twice as much as we make today with less labor, the purpose of humanity is not just to sit behind a counter and sell things, you know?" - "There will be challenges because the rate of change will be faster in these next 20 years than it’s been before". Look, I am no freaking expert, but I think he meant “we all shall prepare for permanent vacation on welfare” Richard Branson said: “I think with the coming on of AI and other things there is certainly a danger of income inequality,” - “The inequality will be caused by the amount of jobs [artificial intelligence] is going to take away and so on,” - “There is no question” technology will eliminate jobs”. So, are you getting the idea here, they are promoting the fact of putting you out of work and on welfare “as something that is already happening and gaining traction”. Please forget all the movie stuff about robots and Ai…etc. And snape out of the dream. Because Ai-powered machines and software are already all over the place, and extremely important. You want to know how important Ai has become. Listen to the Russians. Here is Russian President Vladimir Putin’s take on Ai: “Artificial intelligence is the future, not only for Russia but for all humankind. It comes with colossal opportunities, but also threats that are difficult to predict. Whoever becomes the leader in this sphere will become the ruler of the world.” Look, AI is already at work all around us, it is affecting everything from our search results to our online dating matches. Recent data shows that the use of Ai in many sectors of business has grown by up to 400% over the last 2 years. There’s no way around it “artificial intelligence is already changing our civilization”. Listen to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said when asked about Ai: “Digital technology, pervasively, is getting embedded in every place: everything, every person, every walk of life is being fundamentally shaped by digital technology — it is happening in our homes, our work, our places of entertainment. It’s amazing to think of the world as a computer. I think that’s the right metaphor for us as we go forward”. I wonder if I can get a job on this big computer he is talking about? Hang on now, I think I forgot to give you a little explanation of what AI is. Here we go, “It is the intelligence demonstrated by machines”. Meaning, programmers and Ai specialists are using sophisticated programming languages and very complex coding to make machines as human-like as possible in terms of “processing information, logic, creativity, behavior and most importantly learning”. Basically, they are creating an artificial human brain “that has no limits, does not forget, and does not need sleep nor coffee breaks”. You might think “that is not all that advanced and corporations have not made massive achievements yet”, but Elon Musk who is obsessed with Ai and invests heavily in it said something rather scary about the secrets of Ai. He said: “I have exposure to the most cutting edge Ai, and I think people should be really concerned by it”. So, what are the economic benefits of Ai? Well, the answer is extremely simple. Ai and automation enable firms to reduce the number of workers while limiting the power of trades unions. Hence saving trillions of dollars annually. Now to the big question, which jobs are expected to disappear in rich countries in the next 20 years, because of Ai and automation? Here is the list. And please forgive me in advance for the bad news. Data entry clerks Administrative and executive secretaries Accounting, bookkeeping, and payroll clerks Accountants and auditors Assembly and factory workers Business services and administration managers Client information and customer service workers General and operations managers Mechanics and machinery repairs Material-recording and stock-keeping clerks Leading philosophers, scientists, activist IT experts, human rights experts, educators, and scholars from around the globe collectively agree that Ai and automation are not the problems. And just like any other “construct or system” that is created by humans, it is the creators and controllers role combined with governmental regulations and policies aka “the social system” that decides the process of implementation, outcome, and final results of any new innovation or system with a wide universal effect. The “Godfather of Deep Learning” Geoffrey Hinton once said about Ai technology: “If you can dramatically increase productivity and make more goodies to go around, that should be a good thing. Whether or not it turns out to be a good thing depends entirely on the social system, and doesn’t depend at all on technology. People are looking at the technology as if the technological advances are a problem. The problem is in the [Social Systems], and whether we’re going to have a social system that shares fairly or one that focuses all the improvement on the 1% and treats the rest of the people like dirt. That’s nothing to do with technology. I hope the rewards will outweigh the downsides, but I don’t know whether they will, and that’s an issue of social systems, not with the technology.” Elon Musk had a say on this issue, he once said: “Got to regulate AI/robotics like we do food, drugs, aircraft & cars. Public risks require public oversight. Getting rid of the FAA won’t make flying safer. They’re there for good reason.” Bill Gates also had a say, he said: “If a human worker does $50,000 of work in a factory, that income is taxed,” - “If a robot comes in to do the same thing, you’d think we’d tax the robot at a similar level.”. He meant taxation as a method for discouraging companies from replacing people with machines. Now check out this fact, The McKinsey Institute estimates that AI may deliver an additional economic output of around US$13 trillion by 2030, increasing global GDP by about 1.2 % annually. This will mainly come from the substitution of labor by automation and increased innovation in products and services. The code words in the last sentence are? Yes, you guessed it right “substitution of labor”. The Academic researcher and writer Nick Bostrom, author of Superintelligence once said: “Before the prospect of an intelligence explosion, we humans are like small children playing with a bomb. Such is the mismatch between the power of our plaything and the immaturity of our conduct. Superintelligence is a challenge for which we are not ready now and will not be ready for a long time. We have little idea when the detonation will occur, though if we hold the device to our ear we can hear a faint ticking sound. As of this moment, all evidence points that Ai is not just a threat to your job, but to life and humanity, because the most advanced Ai and robots in existence are somewhere in the world superpowers’ military warehouses. transcript: The AI music world has just hit an interesting snag, and that is that the U.S. copyright, and this has been backed up by the Supreme Court, has ruled that AI music is not eligible for copyright. In order for it to be eligible for copyright, it has to at least have human contributions to it, and those AI contributions need to be disclosed. That means that if somebody makes like an AI song and then sings over that AI song, the AI portion of that song is not copyrightable, which means that that anybody can use it, which will change the landscape of how these things are done. If a company uses an AI song for an ad, they have no protections over who later uses that AI song. I think this is super interesting because it does lend some protections to people who create actual music. For example think about it this way If that was not copywritten right If that was not protected you could then use that same theme for your porno music And McDonald's would be able to do nothing about that. And I think one of the most vulnerable groups to AI being used was people who did sync licensing. Because it's just obviously so easy to just prompt AI to make the sync song that you want and not pay somebody for their reasonable work. But if you can't have copyright protections over that sync work, it devalues that music for use as a brand tool. transcript: A stationary smartphone sitting on a desk generates zero valuable movement data for a tech company. It's quiet, predictable, and commercially useless. But when a densely populated area is bombarded, people panic. They run. They make frantic calls to find their families. In an instant that exact same device produces a massive, highly profitable wave of geoloccation and communication data. Data brokers have openly discussed vacuuming up this exact type of panic-driven data from the war in Gaza. They extract the digital footprint of a fleeing population and use it as raw material to train their proprietary AI models. Once trained, these algorithms don't stay in the war zone. They get shopped around to foreign governments by powerful political networking groups like the Tony Blair Institute acting as highle brokers. The ultimate buyer in one recent deal, the British National Health Service. Software trained directly on the chaotic movement and suffering of people in Gaza was sold for a billion pounds to help manage hospital emergencies in the UK. The arms trade has evolved into a data extraction industry. It captures the digital exhaust of human suffering and refineses it into global enterprise software. This data pipeline runs in both directions. Major US tech platforms provide the literal infrastructure, the data centers, and the computing power that enables Israel's mass surveillance across Gaza and the West Bank. Take Unit 8200, Israel's intelligence division. They track vulnerabilities in apps like WhatsApp to monitor which family chats Palestinians belong to, turning communication into targeting coordinates. Because US platforms hold a monopoly, avoiding them is impossible. Civilians unknowingly opt in to a massive monitoring net. The people engineering this architecture aren't neutral observers. Palunteer's founder is a far-right billionaire who aggressively funds political figures supporting the war effort, playing a key role in backing Donald Trump's campaigns. That financial backing extends right to the current vice president who came up directly as a protege within that exact same tech billionaire network. The executives controlling the world's primary digital infrastructure are active ideological participants using their platforms and wealth to shape the execution of global conflicts. But far away from those sterile server farms, the reality on the ground looks entirely different. With the local economy completely decimated by air strikes, the digital global market is the absolute only way left for Palestinian IT graduates and freelancers to earn an income and keep their families fed. Connecting to that market requires extreme physical risks. Young developers are forced to climb high onto unstable piles of rubble, holding their phones up against the sky just to catch a fleeting EIM signal and respond to international clients. Even when they find a signal, the connection is incredibly fragile. Constant power outages and a severe lack of safe co-working spaces make it nearly impossible to provide the day in dayout consistency that international employers demand. It creates a brutal paradox. The exact same digital infrastructure being used to monitor and target you from the sky is also the only lifeline keeping you alive on the ground. In the West, protesting or deleting an app is an accessible political statement, but boycotting is a privilege. People inside Gaza simply cannot afford to disconnect from an internet controlled entirely by the state actively bombing them. The psychological toll is immense. Palestinian software developers find themselves forced to study and work using AI models built by the exact same companies partnered with the military, destroying their neighborhoods. And the pressure never really stops. Even during a ceasefire, the violence continues through the constant unseen buzz of surveillance drones, trapping the population in an open air panopticon and leaving them with massive unprocessed trauma. This system of digital imperialism extends far beyond Gaza. It relies on passively siphoning data from all of our phones to consolidate power within a few corporate monopolies that answer to no government. The way out involves a deliberate migration. By slowly moving our daily communications to open-source non US alternatives like Signal or Upscroll, we can begin starving these systems of their most valuable resource. Since big tech's influence is fueled by our attention, moving toward alternative digital infrastructure transforms personal privacy into a direct act of geopolitical resistance.
